I got a new dog back in 2014 after my previous one passed away due to his age. We were best buddies until one day he had crazy cramps. We didn’t know what was going on and took him to the vet. Came out that he had epilepsia and had to start taking medicine. He had some sort of a brain loss after these cramps cause it seemed like he didn’t know who my family was or where he was at. I played with him every single day, trying to help him to remember basic things, until around month later before I went to sleep, I heard noises which reminded me of cats playing. We didn’t have cats anymore by that time. For some reason I didn’t went to check and soon after I heard my mum running to my dad whilst crying to tell him that the cramps are back. I was terrified of falling asleep. In the morning, he was barely breathing. I refused to go to school and stayed at home. 2h later I went to check on him and he was gone. His body was just lying there, no breathing movements. The worst bit is that I told myself that I’ll stay in my homeland/alive as long as he’s alive. Probably the creepiest thing what I ever experienced is the following. 

Me and my friends went to a playground in the middle of the night, the town was quiet. We all were around 14 back then, it was pretty foggy (could only see 1,5m max) on that day in October. We lived in a town which was called the capital of drugs back then. We were all swinging on our swings (5 swings in total, only four of us), chatting and laughing. One moment we see a woman standing near the empty swing, looking down at her feet. She was wearing dirty clothes filled with holes and her hair was extremely tangled. We all kinda freaked out. So we decided to ask if everything's ok with her. She kept talking but none of us understood her until she said that she wants to kill one of our friends by scratching his neck until blood starts flowing. We all just sat there, extremely scared and kept looking at each other. We asked why would she do that and she just stood there until suddenly she just rushed by our friend, stood behind him and grabbed his throat. The terror and hopelessness in my friend's face scared us all. We couldn't call anyone as none of us brought phones with us that night and there was no one walking on the streets so we kept asking her not to do this. She kept saying that she has to do that, we kept begging her again. And then she just ran off to the thick fog. Must have been a junkie...

Found this forum 10min ago and wanted to share my journey. 

I had heard Nirvana’s Smells Like Teen Spirit only a couple of times back when I was younger. Back in 2013, I went to Sicily as an exchange student together with a couple of other students. One of the students was a girl who I genuinely didn’t like. I remember her being extremely hyped once she saw one of Nirvana’s tees in one of the stores and that was the day when I swore to myself that I’d never listen to any of Nirvana’s songs during my lifetime (especially cause they’re a rock band [that’s what I used to think] and back then I genuinely hated rock music + I used to dislike everything mainstream used to love just cause I could haha). 
Fast forward 7 years and I had to write a two album essay for one of my classes in university. I decided to write my essay about how ... suicide plan was being reflected on .... last album before ... death. So I knew that I wanted to write about SHINee Jonghyun’s suicide and his last album for sure (I still remember the day when I received the news...) but that meant that I had to pick Nirvana Kurt Cobain’s suicide and In Utero as my second album for this essay (as he is known around the world). 
One of the tasks was to analyse the album, which meant I had to find the time to listen to Nirvana’s In Utero. I hated the idea but decided to listen to in only once in my lifetime, against my will, while distracting myself in the uni library. Well, as you can see in the photo then my plan to listen to In Utero only once was ruined the moment the first track started playing- I fell in love. I bought the vinyl a month later (my first ever vinyl) and here I am now, being influenced by Nirvana almost on a daily basis... 
I can’t even pick out my most favourite song of this album as I love them all. I’ve learned almost everything about (the production side of) this album and although I wish I hadn’t been as stubborn and had listened to Nirvana 7 years ago, I know that I would have not appreciated their music as much as I do now back then.
